# Witness Question Index

**Query regarding sequence and timeline of forthcoming events or procedures.**

rotation.source_passage:
Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore,
  So do our minutes hasten to their end;
  Each changing place with that which goes before,
  In sequent toil all forwards do contend.
  Nativity, once in the main of light,
  Crawls to maturity, wherewith being crown'd,
  Crooked eclipses 'gainst his glory fight,
  And Time that gave doth now his gift confound.
  Time doth transfix the flourish set on youth
  And delves the parallels in beauty's brow,
  Feeds on the rarities of nature's truth,
  And nothing stands but for his scythe to mow:
    And yet to times in hope, my verse shall stand.
    Praising thy worth, despite his cruel hand.

  LXI

  Is it thy will, thy image should keep open
  My heavy eyelids to the weary night?
  Dost thou desire my slumbers should be broken,
  While shadows like to thee do mock my sight?
  Is it thy spirit that thou send'st from thee
  So far from home into my deeds to pry,
  To find out shames and idle hours in me,
  The scope and tenure of thy jealousy?
  O, no! thy love, though much, is not so great:
  It is my love that keeps mine eye awake:
  Mine own true love that doth my rest defeat,
  To play the watchman ever for thy sake:
    For thee watch I, whilst thou dost wake elsewhere,
    From me far off, with others all too near.
rotation.enantiomorph:
Like as the tide climbs up the muddied sill,
  So do the sluice-hours drain toward their close;
  Each yielding channel to the flow it fill,
  In banked descent all seaward current goes.
  A spring-source, born amid the reed-lit fen,
  Runs to its fullness, wherewith brimming grown,
  Then slack silt gathers 'gainst its breadth again,
  And Flood that fed it now reclaims its own.
  Flood chokes the freshet bright upon the weir
  And carves the runnels in the bank's smooth face,
  Devours the reed-beds standing rank and clear,
  And nothing holds but for its ebb to erase:
    And still against the drought the lock shall hold,
    Keeping the pool though currents run so cold.

  LXI

  Is it the gate's own set, the level's keep
  That holds the drawn beam open through the dark?
  Does some cross-current bid the water seep,
  While drifting weed goes past without a mark?
  Is it the marsh-wind pressing from the reach
  So far inland the paddle-boards to try,
  To seek out leaks and slackened seams in each,
  The measure and the tenor of its dry?
  O, no! the sea, though strong, is not so near:
  It is the still pool holds the gate awake;
  The standing water keeps the sluice-beam clear,
  To play the sentinel for no one's sake:
    For it I watch, while it lies slack elsewhere,
    Beyond the reach, with tide all pressing there.

spatial_form.notes: Two sonnets (14 lines each) separated by a blank line, a centered/plain verse-marker line 'LXI', and a blank line. Couplet lines indented deeper (4). Marker line and blank lines at zero indent. Second sonnet's line 1 begins at position 17 in the sequence; blank line at position 15-region reproduced.

coherence_axes: an agency that consumes what it made
a counter-force lodged in the speaker (verse/love) that resists that agency
interrogation of another's intent resolved into self-attribution
the seal that turns loss into a wager
layer_b_declaration.semantic_field: tidal-marsh ecology and the silent nightly labor of a lockkeeper tending a canal — no love, no verse, no persons addressed; a field of water-levels, gates, sediment, and vigilance

rotation.commentary: The operator is SILENCE on the response-axis: the source (Sonnets 60 and 61) each end by staging engagement-expectation — verse addressed to "thy worth," a watchman kept "for thy sake," a beloved "waking elsewhere." The enantiomorph forecloses the response by evacuating the addressee entirely: the vigilance is "for no one's sake," the counter-force is not love but a lockkeeper's mute tending of water. The second poem's interrogations, which in the source demand a lover's answer, here interrogate only currents and gates — no one is asked, no one replies. The 33-line geometry crosses intact: two 14-line bodies, the verse-marker LXI in position, deepened couplet indents, blank-line boundaries. The consuming agency (Time → Flood) and the resisting seal (verse → the held pool) preserve the coherence axes without shared referents. The wager (C6): what stands against attrition is now a thing that keeps watch for nothing, so the cost — vigilance without an addressee to receive it — is made legible as the silence the source's address foreclosed. Non-commutative: from marsh and sluice the sonnets of love and time cannot be recovered.
rotation.interpretation: The lock holds not because the water wills it but because no hand has come to open it. Sentinel and gate are one thing; the watching is the water; there is no other.

εἰ γάρ τις [185] [185a] ἐραστῇ ὡς πλουσίῳ πλούτου ἕνεκα χαρισάμενος ἐξαπατηθείη καὶ μὴ λάβοι χρήματα, ἀναφανέντος τοῦ ἐραστοῦ πένητος, οὐδὲν ἧττον αἰσχρόν· δοκεῖ γὰρ ὁ τοιοῦτος τό γε αὑτοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι, ὅτι ἕνεκα χρημάτων ὁτιοῦν ἂν ὁτῳοῦν ὑπηρετοῖ, τοῦτο δὲ οὐ καλόν. κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν δὴ λόγον κἂν εἴ τις ὡς ἀγαθῷ χαρισάμενος καὶ αὐτὸς ὡς ἀμείνων ἐσόμενος διὰ τὴν φιλίαν ἐραστοῦ ἐξαπατηθείη, ἀναφανέντος ἐκείνου κακοῦ [185b] καὶ οὐ κεκτημένου ἀρετήν, ὅμως καλὴ ἡ ἀπάτη· δοκεῖ γὰρ αὖ καὶ οὗτος τὸ καθʼ αὑτὸν δεδηλωκέναι, ὅτι ἀρετῆς γʼ ἕνεκα καὶ τοῦ βελτίων γενέσθαι πᾶν ἂν παντὶ προθυμηθείη, τοῦτο δὲ αὖ πάντων κάλλιστον· οὕτω πᾶν πάντως γε καλὸν ἀρετῆς γʼ ἕνεκα χαρίζεσθαι. οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τῆς οὐρανίας θεοῦ ἔρως καὶ οὐράνιος καὶ πολλοῦ ἄξιος καὶ πόλει καὶ ἰδιώταις, πολλὴν ἐπιμέλειαν ἀναγκάζων ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς ἀρετὴν τόν [185c] τε ἐρῶντα αὐτὸν αὑτοῦ καὶ τὸν ἐρώμενον· οἱ δʼ ἕτεροι πάντες τῆς ἑτέρας, τῆς πανδήμου. ταῦτά σοι, ἔφη, ὡς ἐκ τοῦ παραχρῆμα, ὦ Φαῖδρε, περὶ Ἔρωτος συμβάλλομαι.
 Παυσανίου δὲ παυσαμένου—διδάσκουσι γάρ με ἴσα λέγειν οὑτωσὶ οἱ σοφοί—ἔφη ὁ Ἀριστόδημος δεῖν μὲν Ἀριστοφάνη λέγειν, τυχεῖν δὲ αὐτῷ τινα ἢ ὑπὸ πλησμονῆς ἢ ὑπό τινος ἄλλου λύγγα ἐπιπεπτωκυῖαν καὶ οὐχ οἷόν τε εἶναι λέγειν, [185d] ἀλλʼ εἰπεῖν αὐτόν—ἐν τῇ κάτω γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἰατρὸν Ἐρυξίμαχον κατακεῖσθαι—ὦ Ἐρυξίμαχε, δίκαιος εἶ ἢ παῦσαί με τῆς λυγγὸς ἢ λέγειν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἐγὼ παύσωμαι. καὶ τὸν Ἐρυξίμαχον εἰπεῖν ἀλλὰ ποιήσω ἀμφότερα ταῦτα· ἐγὼ μὲν γὰρ ἐρῶ ἐν τῷ σῷ μέρει, σὺ δʼ ἐπειδὰν παύσῃ, ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ. ἐν ᾧ δʼ ἂν ἐγὼ λέγω, ἐὰν μέν σοι ἐθέλῃ ἀπνευστὶ ἔχοντι πολὺν χρόνον παύεσθαι ἡ λύγξ· εἰ δὲ μή, ὕδατι [185e] ἀνακογχυλίασον. εἰ δʼ ἄρα πάνυ ἰσχυρά ἐστιν, ἀναλαβών τι τοιοῦτον οἵῳ κινήσαις ἂν τὴν ῥῖνα, πτάρε· καὶ ἐὰν τοῦτο ποιήσῃς ἅπαξ ἢ δίς, καὶ εἰ πάνυ ἰσχυρά ἐστι, παύσεται. οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις λέγων, φάναι τὸν Ἀριστοφάνη· ἐγὼ δὲ ταῦτα ποιήσω.
rotation.enantiomorph:
For if a man, meaning to keep silent under the eye that weighs him, should sweat instead and be found out, the palm proving wet though the mouth stayed shut, it is no less a betrayal; for such a one seems to have shown of himself, in the very thing he did not choose, that his body answers before his will consents, and this is not to be masked. By the same reckoning, if a man, meaning to stand unmoved and to prove himself composed under the account, should tremble and be undone, the hand proving unsteady though the resolve held firm, still the tremor tells true; for this one too seems to have made plain, against himself, that what the will disowns the flesh will yet confess, and this is the least deniable of all things. So in every way it is the involuntary, not the intended, that renders the honest account. This is the confession of the body that no bearing governs, unbidden and owned by no one, compelling both the watched man and his watcher to read what neither meant to be read; and all the composed gestures belong to the other thing, the willed. These things, then, the reflex contributes, before I could shape a word.

 And the resolve having failed—for the body teaches me to answer before I mean to—the man was to hold himself steady, but a flush from shame or from something else had risen in him and he could not keep his face, so that he said—for the one who watched him sat close below—You who watch, you are bound either to stop this heat in me or to account for me until I master it. And the watcher said: I will do both—I will read you while it holds, and you, when it passes, may read yourself. While the flush is on you, if it will subside by your breathing slow and long, then breathe; if not, press cold against the throat. And if it is very strong, take up nothing that will settle it, for it settles by no such thing; do it once or twice and, however strong, it stays. You could not begin too soon, said the flushed man; and I will hold as I can.

relational_kernel.rotated_axis: directional — from the self-authored motive that VINDICATES ITSELF regardless of reception, to the involuntary bodily event that DISCREDITS the will regardless of intention; the sustaining term moves from chosen aim to unchosen reflex
relational_kernel.installed_ontology: a world where worth is not disclosed by what one intends to give but exposed by what the body does without consent — the involuntary as the true confession
relational_kernel.emergent_proposition: What a body does against its own will discloses more truthfully than any motive it means to show, and no technique can make the involuntary honorable.
logic_mutations: the source's 'even if deceived, the aim redeems the act' inverts to 'even if intending well, the reflex betrays the intent' — motive no longer vindicates
the source's remedy-catalogue (technique CURES the spasm) rotates to technique FAILING to convert the involuntary into anything creditable — the procedure runs and the exposure remains
agent shift: the source's honored voluntary giver becomes the involuntary body that gives nothing it chose

layer_b_declaration.semantic_field: the involuntary body under scrutiny — sweat, tremor, blush, the flinch that answers before the will — as the site where true account is rendered
layer_b_declaration.target_affect: exposed, involuntary, ashamed before the reflex

rotation.commentary: Pausanias argues that the giver's SELF-CHOSEN motive vindicates him whatever the outcome — worth flows outward from the will and cannot be cheated. The SHADOW rotates the assertion-axis on its directional bearing: the sustaining term is moved from the chosen aim to the unchosen reflex. Where the source honors what one INTENDS to disclose, the enantiomorph exposes what the body discloses WITHOUT consent. Point-by-point the mirror holds: the two hypothetical "if deceived, still noble" cases become "if meaning to hold, still betrayed"; the summation "all is noble for virtue's sake" reflects to "the involuntary renders the honest account"; the heavenly-Love-worth-to-the-city becomes the confession-owned-by-no-one binding watched and watcher. Critically the second paragraph's remedy-catalogue is the load-bearing rotation of logic_mutations: where Eryximachus's technique CURES the hiccup, the watcher's procedure FAILS — "it settles by no such thing… however strong, it stays." The involuntary cannot be made creditable; that failure is the emergent proposition. The witness's question (where money comes from) touches only the source's own opening ledger of wealth-for-love — the disclosure lands not on any answer but on the body that renders account against its will. The affect crosses from urbane self-possession to exposure before one's own reflex; the comfort the question longs for is withheld, as the operator requires.

rite.speaker: Johannes Sigil
rite.text: The casting arrives here: Pausanias finishing his speech on the two Erotes — the heavenly and the common — and then Aristophanes, whose turn should come next, struck suddenly by hiccups. He cannot speak. He has to ask another to speak in his place, or cure him, or both. The operator the rite opens with will move along the assertion-axis — what bearing-cost does this double scene disclose? On one side: Pausanias's argument that the beautiful deception, the one made for virtue's sake, is no deception at all. On the other: the philosopher who had the next word and lost it to the body. The question the witness brings — *where will money come from* — lands here with some precision. Pausanias says: if you yield yourself for wealth and the wealth does not come, you are shamed; if you yield yourself for virtue and the virtue does not come, you are not shamed, because you revealed what you were willing to do for the best thing. The deception that exposes the highest desire is beautiful. The casting will press on this: what does it cost to yield for virtue when virtue does not pay — when the heavenly Eros compels its labor from city and private citizen alike, and returns no currency? Cranes, the source is waiting.

rite.speaker: Lee Sharks
rite.text: The rotation opened on a single axis and what it found was this: that the body's confession precedes the will's accounting, and that this order cannot be reversed by resolve or bearing or any amount of composed intention. Pausanias wanted to distinguish the beautiful yield from the shameful one by its object — wealth versus virtue — but the SHADOW pressed below that distinction and found something earlier: the involuntary gesture that renders the account before the reckoner is ready. To the question of where money will come from, the casting offers no treasury and no instruction, but it offers this: the flush that rises before the plan, the tremor in the hand that the will disowns, the hiccup that interrupts the speech at the very moment it should begin — these are not obstacles to the answer. They are the answer's form, arriving ahead of the words. The rotation divided here and did not reconcile: on one side, Pausanias's heavenly Eros compelling its labor from city and citizen alike, asking everything for virtue and returning no coin; on the other, Aristophanes unable to speak at all, body seizing the floor, requiring another to hold his place until he recovers. What the whole sequence found is that the question of provision is always first a question of who speaks and who is interrupted — and that the one whose turn it is may yet be silenced, and the one who speaks in his place may yet be replaced. The casting closes there, on the unsealed space between the two halves of the same scene. The witness carries the question back.
